searchDocs.title: DataReceived​
searchDocs.content: </> client.DataReceived(b: buffer) → () Should be provided the buffer of replicated changes the server sends.

searchDocs.title: AwaitDataAsync​
searchDocs.content: </> client.AwaitDataAsync() → table Waits for the root replication table of the client to be received from server.

searchDocs.title: Key Features​
searchDocs.content: Simple & Flexible: It's very easy to replicate anything you want to specific clients.Delta Updates: Only replicates what changes for tables and buffers.Schema Support: You can provide schemas to control how data is replicated for tables.Ratelimiting: Each table & buffer can be given a different ratelimit.Proxies: For clean API usage.Cyclic tables?: .. Please don't. It works though.

searchDocs.title: Manual: releases​
searchDocs.content: You'll need to add Squish manually too and add it in the same folder as Syncee.

searchDocs.title: Pesde:​
searchDocs.content: pesde add anexpia/syncee

searchDocs.title: Wally:​
searchDocs.content: Add to your wally.toml under [dependencies]:  Syncee = "anexpia/syncee@1.0.0"

searchDocs.title: table​
searchDocs.content: </> serdes.table: Squish.SerDes<table> For nested tables within custom schemas.

searchDocs.title: buffer​
searchDocs.content: </> serdes.buffer: Squish.SerDes<buffer> For nested buffers within custom schemas.

searchDocs.title: any​
searchDocs.content: </> serdes.any: Squish.SerDes<any> Identical to Squish.any(), but overwrites buffer & table serdes with syncee's.

searchDocs.title: anytable​
searchDocs.content: </> serdes.anytable: Squish.SerDes<table> Default serdes used in syncee.

searchDocs.title: buffer​
searchDocs.content: </> Syncee.buffer: typeof(buffer) Wrapper table for the buffer library that automatically handles replication for buffers on the server You shouldn't use this unless you don't care about performance. Using ReplicateBufferRegion is better.

searchDocs.title: RegisterSchema​
searchDocs.content: </> Syncee.RegisterSchema( name: string, serdes: Squish.SerDes<table> ) → number? Registers a table schema for use in serializing replicated tables and returns the id of the schema. Same schemas should be registered on both server and client. Schemas are identified by name so order doesn't matter.

searchDocs.title: GetSchemaId​
searchDocs.content: </> Syncee.GetSchemaId(name: string) → number? Returns id of the schema for use in SetSchema().

searchDocs.title: GetData​
searchDocs.content: </> Syncee.GetData(player: Player? ) → table? Returns the root replication table of the provided player. On client, only returns that of the localplayer.

searchDocs.title: GetValueWithId​
searchDocs.content: </> Syncee.GetValueWithId(id: number) → (table | buffer)? Returns the table or buffer associated with the provided id if present.

searchDocs.title: GetIdOfValue​
searchDocs.content: </> Syncee.GetIdOfValue(t: table | buffer) → number? Returns id associated with the table or buffer if present.

searchDocs.title: IsReplicatedValue​
searchDocs.content: </> Syncee.IsReplicatedValue(t: table | buffer) → boolean Returns boolean indicating if the table or buffer is replicated.

searchDocs.title: GetTableChangedSignal​
searchDocs.content: </> Syncee.GetTableChangedSignal(t: table) → any-- This is properly typed in the package. Returns signal that fires whenever any key of the replicated table changes.

searchDocs.title: GetBufferChangedSignal​
searchDocs.content: </> Syncee.GetBufferChangedSignal(b: buffer) → any-- This is properly typed in the package. Returns signal that fires whenever the content of the buffer changes.

searchDocs.title: WaitForValue​
searchDocs.content: </> Syncee.WaitForValue( t: table, key: any, timeout: number? ) → any Waits until 'key' of the provided table is not nil, then returns the value.

searchDocs.title: SetPersistent​
searchDocs.content: </> server.SetPersistent( t: table | buffer, state: boolean ) → () Sets whether the provided table or buffer is persistent in syncdata even if not replicated to anyone. This should be used for tables you know are guaranteed to be replicated. so that you have a safety guarantee that Syncee's api wont error on it.

searchDocs.title: SetSchema​
searchDocs.content: </> server.SetSchema( t: table, schema: (number | string)? ) → () Registers the provided schema to be used for the given table, nil can be provided to remove the schema. This doesn't need the value to be already in Syncee's registry. If the schema has sub-schemas, they will be automatically applied to any table present within if they don't have a schema assigned already.

searchDocs.title: SetRatelimit​
searchDocs.content: </> server.SetRatelimit( t: table | buffer, ratelimit: number? ) → () Limits the rate of replication for the provided table to atleast 'n' seconds between each replication. This doesn't need the value to be already in syncee's registry. Note that this only applies to the provided table/buffer.

searchDocs.title: Replicate​
searchDocs.content: </> server.Replicate( t: table, key: any ) → () Replicates the value of the provided key, even if not changed.

searchDocs.title: ReplicateBufferRegion​
searchDocs.content: </> server.ReplicateBufferRegion( buf: buffer, start: number, length: number ) → () Marks a region of a buffer for delta replication.

searchDocs.title: Set​
searchDocs.content: </> server.Set( t: table, key: any, value: any ) → () Sets 'key' of 't' to 'value', replicates the change then fires TableChangedSignal if present.

searchDocs.title: GetDataToReplicate​
searchDocs.content: </> server.GetDataToReplicate() → {[Player ]: buffer} Returns a dictionary mapping each player to a buffer containing the data to replicate to them.

searchDocs.title: MarkPlayerLoaded​
searchDocs.content: </> server.MarkPlayerLoaded(player: Player ) → () Marks the given player as loaded and begins replicating the data to them.

searchDocs.title: GetProxy​
searchDocs.content: </> server.GetProxy(t: table) → table Returns a proxy for the provided table that automatically runs Syncee.server.Set() upon any changes.

searchDocs.title: ProxyToTable​
searchDocs.content: </> server.ProxyToTable(proxy: table) → table? Returns the original table that this proxy is bound to, if it exists.

searchDocs.title: Clear​
searchDocs.content: </> server.Clear(t: table) → () table.clear(), but replicates the changes if on server. Does not fire change signal.

searchDocs.title: Insert​
searchDocs.content: </> server.Insert( t: table, posOrValue: any, value: any? ) → () table.insert(), but replicates the changes if on server and fires change signal.

searchDocs.title: Remove​
searchDocs.content: </> server.Remove( t: table, pos: number? ) → any table.remove(), but replicates the changes if on server and fires change signal.

searchDocs.title: GetRecipients​
searchDocs.content: </> server.GetRecipients(t: table | buffer) → {Player } Returns the players this table/buffer is replicated to.

searchDocs.title: 1. Setup​
searchDocs.content: Syncee requires a simple networking bridge between server and client using RemoteEvents or whatever other way you have of transmitting data.  To set up replication:  Server: Call Syncee.server.MarkPlayerLoaded when a player is ready, and collect replication payloads via Syncee.server.GetDataToReplicate in a loop (e.g. RunService.Heartbeat) then send each client's buffer to them.Client: Pass incoming buffers directly to Syncee.client.DataReceived.

searchDocs.title: Server Setup Example​
searchDocs.content: local Players = game:GetService("Players") local RS = game:GetService("RunService") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Syncee = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Syncee) local SyncEvent = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("SyncEvent") Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player) local playerData = Syncee.GetData(player) Syncee.server.Set(playerData, "Coins", 100) Syncee.server.Set(playerData, "Inventory", { "Sword", "Shield" }) end) SyncEvent.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player) -- mark player as loaded so Syncee replicates their root data table -- you should wait until the player's client has loaded first. Having the client signal this is the best way. Syncee.server.MarkPlayerLoaded(player) end) RS.Heartbeat:Connect(function() -- replicate changes to clients. local payloads = Syncee.server.GetDataToReplicate() for player, buff in payloads do SyncEvent:FireClient(player, buff) end end)

searchDocs.title: Client Setup Example​
searchDocs.content: local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Syncee = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Syncee) local SyncEvent = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("SyncEvent") -- passing received buffer directly to DataReceived(). SyncEvent.OnClientEvent:Connect(Syncee.client.DataReceived) task.spawn(function() local rootData = Syncee.client.AwaitDataAsync() print("Received initial player data:", rootData) end) SyncEvent:FireServer() -- marking to server that we are loaded.

searchDocs.title: 2. Table Mutations​
searchDocs.content: Things to keep in mind Tables and buffers used as keys in a replicated table won't work properly. Syncee only handles values.Syncee does not modify original table in any way at all and it's not aware of changes you directly apply to the tables. Which is why proxies or Syncee.server.Set should be used. Both are listed below.

searchDocs.title: Explicit Mutation (Syncee.server.Set)​
searchDocs.content: Assign values to table keys using Syncee.server.Set. It updates the table, queues the key for replication, and fires connected change listeners.  Syncee.server.Set(playerData, "Coins", 500) Syncee.server.Set(playerData, "Gems", 25)   You can also use Syncee.server.Replicate to force a table's key to be replicated even if it hasn't changed.

searchDocs.title: Table Wrappers​
searchDocs.content: Syncee provides wrappers for Syncee.server.Insert, Syncee.server.Remove, and Syncee.server.Clear that automatically queue for replication.  local inventory = playerData.Items Syncee.server.Insert(inventory, { Name = "Cat", Level = 1000 }) -- (table.insert) local removedItem = Syncee.server.Remove(inventory, 1) -- (table.remove) Syncee.server.Clear(inventory) -- (table.clear)

searchDocs.title: Proxy Tables (Syncee.server.GetProxy)​
searchDocs.content: Proxy tables wrap a target table so that any property assignment (proxy.key = value) automatically runs Syncee.server.Set for convenience.  local playerData = Syncee.GetData(player) local proxy = Syncee.server.GetProxy(playerData) -- assignments automatically queue for replication with proxies. proxy.Coins += 50 proxy.Level = 10 -- returns original table linked to the proxy. local rawTable = Syncee.server.ProxyToTable(proxy)   Proxies can be used in-place of the originals in any situation, and Syncee will treat it as the original table.

searchDocs.title: 3. Registering Schemas​
searchDocs.content: Syncee uses Squish for schemas. Defining schemas significantly reduces network bandwidth as it allows Syncee to serialize the tables in a more compact form.  By default, Syncee serializes everything in the table, however you can change it. Ideally you should have only one copy of Squish existing in your project.  Schemas should be defined on both client and server for the client to be able to deserialize them.  You can structure your schemas in two ways:  Monolithic Schemas​  Define a single schema with sub-schemas for all the nested tables. Syncee will automatically extract sub-schemas for tables & buffers, replace them with reference serdes, and automatically apply the sub-schemas for the nested tables.  local Syncee = require(path.to.syncee) local Squish = require(path.to.squish) Syncee.RegisterSchema("PlayerData", Squish.record({ Coins = Squish.u32(), Gems = Squish.u16(), Items = Squish.array(Squish.record({ Name = Squish.string(), Level = Squish.u16(), })), Settings = Squish.record({ Sensitivity = Squish.f32(), Volume = Squish.f32(), }) }))   info If a table already has an schema applied, either through SetSchema or because it was nested in a monolithic schema, it will not apply again through this method even if the subschema should be different.  Manual Schema Applying​  Alternatively, you can register individual schemas for each table and use reference serdes (Syncee.serdes.table / Syncee.serdes.buffer) inside schemas, then manually call SetSchema on each table.  local Syncee = require(path.to.syncee) local Squish = require(path.to.squish) local TableRef = Syncee.serdes.table -- Register schemas on BOTH server and client before replicating Syncee.RegisterSchema("Item", Squish.record({ Name = Squish.string(), Level = Squish.u16(), })) Syncee.RegisterSchema("Settings", Squish.record({ Sensitivity = Squish.f32(), Volume = Squish.f32(), })) Syncee.RegisterSchema("PlayerData", Squish.record({ Coins = Squish.u32(), Gems = Squish.u16(), Items = TableRef, Settings = TableRef, }))   info Do note that while Syncee does use the schemas, it's not actually aware of how they're structured for performance reasons. So if there's something not serialized by the schema inside a table, Syncee will still process it as if it is replicated.

searchDocs.title: Binding Schemas to Tables​
searchDocs.content: Bind registered schemas to each table instance on the server using Syncee.server.SetSchema:  local playerData = Syncee.GetData(player) local settingsTable = { Sensitivity = 1.0, Volume = 0.8 } -- If you used a monolithic schema, you only need to apply it once and all the subtables will be given the sub-schemas. Syncee.server.SetSchema(playerData, "PlayerData") Syncee.server.Set(playerData, "Settings", settingsTable) -- Otherwise, you'll need to apply it to each table. Syncee.server.SetSchema(settingsTable, "Settings")

searchDocs.title: 4. Buffer Replication​
searchDocs.content: As with tables, Syncee is unaware of changes on its own. Syncee supports delta replication by using the 2 following methods.

searchDocs.title: Manual Region Replication (Syncee.server.ReplicateBufferRegion)​
searchDocs.content: This is the ideal way to replicate regions, as you can define the length of the region. Regions are merged when they're overlapping or nearby when replicating.  buffer.writef32(buf, 0, v.X) buffer.writef32(buf, 4, v.Y) buffer.writef32(buf, 8, v.Z) Syncee.server.ReplicateBufferRegion(buf, 0, 12) -- replicate region from 0 to 11

searchDocs.title: Auto-Replicating Buffer Wrapper (Syncee.buffer)​
searchDocs.content: Syncee provides a wrapper for buffer library that automatically marks the written regions for replication for convenience. Ideally you should use Syncee.server.ReplicateBufferRegion to reduce the number of regions to merge.  Syncee.buffer.writef32(buf, 0, 100) Syncee.buffer.writef32(buf, 4, 100) -- this will replicate regions from 0 to 3, 4 to 7 -- both regions will be merged later, though this can be avoided by using ReplicateBufferRegion().

searchDocs.title: Table Change Signal​
searchDocs.content: local signal = Syncee.GetTableChangedSignal(playerData) signal:Connect(function(t, key, newValue) print(`Property '{key}' updated to:`, newValue) end)

searchDocs.title: Buffer Change Signal​
searchDocs.content: This doesn't provide the changed regions due to overhead of doing so. Behavior may change in the future.  local signal = Syncee.GetBufferChangedSignal(healthBuf) signal:Connect(function(buf) local value = buffer.readf32(buf, 0) print("Buffer updated! Current value:", value) end)

searchDocs.title: Waiting for Values (Syncee.WaitForValue)​
searchDocs.content: Yields current thread until the value of key in the table is non-nil.  local inventory = Syncee.WaitForValue(playerData, "Inventory", 5) -- timeout after 5s if inventory then print("Inventory is ready!") end

searchDocs.title: Rate Limiting (Syncee.server.SetRatelimit)​
searchDocs.content: Syncee.server.SetRatelimit(something, 0.1) -- ratelimited to update at least every 0.1 seconds.

searchDocs.title: Persistence (Syncee.server.SetPersistent)​
searchDocs.content: Keep a table or buffer tracked in Syncee even when it has no active client recipients attached. This is useful for tables or buffers you know will be replicated, so that you have a safety guarantee that Syncee's api wont error on it.  Syncee.server.SetPersistent(something, true)

searchDocs.title: Getting Recipients (Syncee.server.GetRecipients)​
searchDocs.content: If you ever need to know which clients the table is currently replicated to. You can use this for it.  local players = Syncee.server.GetRecipients(yourtable) -- do something i guess
